tasks.short: Store and retrieve catalog and lecture notes

steps.what: Prepare classification and catalog information using computers
Review the catalog information and the lecture notes
Store the accepted notes and other related documents
Retrieve stored documents by the known identifier

tasks.design: The assistant prepares classification and catalog information and lecture notes on the computer. {DOCS} stores the note only after the assistant accepts that version, and retrieves a document when its identifier is already known. Store and retrieve are separate. A missing identifier is not searched by guesswork, and a blank note is not stored.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant saved and later hunted for the same note under shifting names.
tasks.enabler_now: A known document identifier can be stored and later fetched as an exact lookup.
tasks.still_hard: Preparing the note, and deciding it is ready, stay with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant does not store a note whose classification they have not checked.
tasks.altitude: Preparation stays. A known document comes back by its identifier, and only an accepted note is stored.

reach.task: Set the classification the note should carry
reach.learn: Which classification the librarian wants on lecture notes.

evidence.claim: A known document identifier can be stored and retrieved exactly. A missing identifier returns nothing. Preparing the note stays manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a note to prepare and ends when it is stored, or when a known identifier is retrieved.
The assistant enters document identifier, classification, and note text. A blank identifier or a blank classification stops the store. Retrieve uses only an identifier already stored.
The store uses the version accepted in the review. Retrieve does not write.
research_questions: How many retrieves failed because the identifier was unknown?

already_counted.description: Preparing classification and catalog information is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a classification on a note the assistant has not yet accepted.

approvals.approved_version: catalog note version the assistant accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: notes are still composed at the screen, and identifiers are often missing. High: known identifiers store and retrieve after review, and preparing the note remains. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select a substitute when a title is unavailable

steps.what: Mark requested materials that are unavailable
Select substitute titles following criteria such as age, education, and interests

tasks.design: When requested materials are unavailable, the assistant selects a substitute using criteria such as age, education, and interests. {DOCS} only marks that the requested title has no available copy. The assistant chooses the substitute. A missing availability stays blank and is not treated as unavailable.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant discovered the gap at the shelf and chose a substitute from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: A copy count can show unavailable without choosing the replacement.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a title that fits the patron stays with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant will not offer a substitute that ignores the age or the interest the patron stated.
tasks.altitude: The choice stays the assistant's. The screen only shows that the requested title is unavailable.

reach.task: Suggest a substitute for a specialist subject
reach.learn: Which subjects the desk should not substitute alone.

evidence.claim: A stored copy count can mark a title unavailable. Selecting a substitute stays with the assistant.

assumptions: The work starts with a request and ends when the assistant has selected a substitute or said there is not a fit.
A holding row has title identifier and available copies, updated at lending. A blank count is left blank and is not treated as zero.
The system does not rank substitutes. No patron score is stored.
unknowns: Which criteria the library expects the desk to apply.
research_questions: How often did the assistant reject the idea that the title was unavailable?

already_counted.description: Selecting a substitute title for the patron is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct an available-copy count after the assistant finds the item on the shelf.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: availability is often blank, so the assistant still checks the shelf and then chooses. High: unavailable titles are marked, and the assistant still selects the substitute. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare library statistics reports from stored counts

tasks.design: The assistant prepares library statistics reports. {DATA_PLATFORM} totals stored counts into a draft. A blank count stays blank and the report is not published. The assistant reviews the draft, and {BI} publishes only the accepted version. No commentary is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant added the counts up and retyped them into the report.
tasks.enabler_now: The counts are stored numbers, so the report is a total.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing that a count cannot be right, and refusing to publish it, stay with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant holds a report whose totals do not match the desk's own tally.

ambition.what: A month with complete counts can be published in the version the assistant accepted, instead of waiting on a retype.

tasks.altitude: Adding up shrinks. The assistant still decides that the report is fit to publish.

reach.task: Ask for a breakdown the standard report does not hold
reach.learn: Which counts the librarian treats as mandatory.

evidence.claim: Stored counts can be totaled into a statistics report. A blank count stops publication. No prose is added.

assumptions: The work starts with the period's counts and ends when the assistant publishes the report or stops it.
A count row has period, measure name, and number, entered by the desk or taken from loan events. A blank number is left blank.
Publication uses the report version accepted in the review. A scheduled total that already runs without the assistant is not counted as their time. This report is one the assistant prepares today.
unknowns: Which measures the library requires on the report.
research_questions: How many reports stopped on a blank count?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the statistics report is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a count the assistant finds wrong before accepting the report.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: counts are often blank, so the assistant still builds the report by hand. High: counts are complete, and the assistant still reviews before publication. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Deliver and retrieve items by cart

steps.what: Deliver items to departments using push carts
Retrieve items from departments using push carts

tasks.design: The assistant delivers and retrieves items by hand with a push cart. Delivering and retrieving are separate walks. No system shortens the trip.
tasks.previous_blocker: The cart round is physical, and it still is.
tasks.enabler_now: No stored field moves the cart.
tasks.still_hard: Loading, walking, and unloading stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant checks the item against the department before leaving it.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. Both rounds stay with the assistant.

reach.task: Confirm the item belongs in that department
reach.learn: Which items must not be left unattended.

evidence.claim: Pushing a cart between departments is physical. A location on a screen does not move the item.

assumptions: The work starts with an item or a request and ends when it has been delivered or brought back.
No new record is required for the walk. Upkeep is zero.
Deliver and retrieve are different walks and are not treated as one shared action.
unknowns: Which departments are on the cart round.
research_questions: How long does a full deliver round take compared with a retrieve round?

already_counted.description: Delivering items by push cart is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: No new upkeep: the cart round adds no record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: every item is still pushed by cart. High: the same two walks remain, with no step removed. No upkeep is added, so the low does not go below zero. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The assistant still meets patrons, shelves items, and handles cash. A record, notice, invoice, or order is written or sent only after the assistant accepts that version.
reach: A librarian receives the question the assistant could not answer from the desk.
A finance colleague receives only an invoice the assistant has accepted.
skills_to_grow: Stop when a required field is blank.
Accept or refuse the exact version before a send or a write.
Keep shelving, cash, and patron conversations in their own hands.
role.ambitious_version: Every item on loan has a location and a due date the desk can trust, and the assistant still decides the exception.
